problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(0,0),(2,0),(2,2).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under a **clockwise** rotation of $\frac{2\pi }{3}$ radians about the origin?

- $(2,-2)$
- $(-1,-\sqrt{3})$
- $(\sqrt{3},0)$

feedback.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-1,0),(1,0),(0,1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under a counterclockwise rotation of ${45}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(-1,-1)$
- $(1,1)$
- $(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})$
feedback.worked_solution:
The rotation matrix ${R}_{\theta }$ represents a rotation of angle $\theta $ counterclockwise about the origin and is given by

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}].
$$

Substituting $\theta ={45}^{∘}$ into the above, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘}) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡({45}^{∘}) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡({45}^{∘}) & \operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the transformation, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the rotation $R$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are 

$$
(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}),\,(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}),\,(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}).
$$

So, the correct answer is "III only."
